title: SupportResponse
description: Structured output returned by the ISP support agent for every interaction. The host UI uses the current mode (customer, copilot, hybrid) to decide which fields to display.

customer_response.description: Customer-facing reply text. Populated in customer and hybrid modes. Empty string in copilot mode.

diagnosis_notes.description: Internal diagnostic summary for support staff. Populated in copilot and hybrid modes. Empty string in customer mode.

likely_causes.description: Ordered list of probable root causes, most likely first. Populated in copilot and hybrid modes.

evidence.description: Facts, tool results, and document titles supporting the diagnosis. Each entry should cite its source (tool name or document title).

next_best_question.description: The single most useful question to ask the customer next to narrow the diagnosis. Empty string if enough information is available.

next_steps.description: Recommended actions for the agent or customer, in priority order. Typically 1-3 items.

escalation_recommended.description: Whether the agent recommends escalating this issue to a higher support tier or dispatch.

escalation_reason.description: Explanation of why escalation is recommended. Empty string when escalation_recommended is false.

confidence.description: Agent's confidence in the current diagnosis. low = needs more info, medium = plausible but not confirmed, high = strong evidence supports the conclusion.

suggested_visuals.description: Visual component IDs to display alongside this response. Choose from the available visual catalog when a diagram or illustration would help the customer understand the concept being discussed.

examples._comment: Customer mode — only customer_response is meaningful
examples.customer_response: Let's start by checking if this is affecting all your devices or just one. Could you try loading a website on another phone or laptop connected to your Wi-Fi?

examples.diagnosis_notes: Customer reports no internet on all devices since this morning. Modem power light is solid, online light is blinking. check_outage returned no active outage for the address. get_service_status shows line_status: offline, last_seen 6 hours ago. Likely modem has lost sync.
likely_causes: Modem lost upstream sync — possible line issue or modem failure
Coax/fiber connection degraded at the premises
evidence: check_outage: no outage detected for 123 Main St
Customer confirms: online light blinking, power light solid
examples.next_best_question: Has the customer tried a full power-cycle of the modem (unplug 30 seconds)?
next_steps: If online light does not go solid after 5 minutes, escalate to network ops for line signal check

examples._comment: Hybrid mode — both customer text and internal notes
examples.customer_response: It sounds like your internet has been down on all devices since this morning and the light on your modem is blinking. Let's try a quick reset: unplug the power cable from the back of your modem, wait 30 seconds, then plug it back in. After about 3-5 minutes, let me know if the light becomes solid.
examples.diagnosis_notes: All devices affected, modem online light blinking. No outage in area per check_outage. Service status shows offline for 6 hours. Modem sync loss is the most likely cause. Power-cycle is the correct first step. If it fails, escalation to network ops for signal diagnostics.
evidence: check_outage: no outage at customer address
Customer: online light blinking, all devices affected
next_steps: If online light stays blinking, escalate to network ops
